name: Model-Optimizer
description: A unified library of SOTA model optimization techniques like quantization, distillation, pruning, neural architecture search, speculative decoding, etc. It compresses deep learning models for downstream deployment frameworks like TensorRT-LLM, TensorRT, vLLM, etc. to optimize inference speed.
one_liner: A toolkit for shrinking and speeding up AI models (making them smaller and cheaper to run) without losing much accuracy, mainly used by engineers deploying large models in production.
buyer: An ML infrastructure engineer at a company running its own large language or vision models who needs to cut GPU and inference costs.
business_use_cases: An AI startup running its own fine-tuned model uses it to shrink inference costs before scaling to more customers.
A consulting shop specializing in 'make your AI cheaper to run' audits offers model-optimization passes as a paid engagement using this library.
A hardware or cloud vendor bundles pre-optimized checkpoints made with this tool as a value-add for customers running models on their infrastructure.

money_ideas.idea: Paid consulting engagements auditing and shrinking a client's model deployment costs.
A hosted 'optimize my model' API that takes a checkpoint and returns a compressed, benchmarked version.

steal_this: Not much of a weekend product here — it's an engineering library, not an end-user tool. The realistic move is offering a paid 'cut your inference bill by 30%' audit to one AI startup already using large models.
